profile.entities: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank Ltd; holding co. Utkarsh CoreInvest Ltd (UCL) — reverse merger of UCL into the bank in progress (2nd motion petition filed with NCLT 5-Apr-2026)
profile.mgmt: Govind Singh (MD & CEO), Sarjukumar Pravin Simaria (CFO), Amit Acharya (CRO), Virender Sharma (Head Micro-Banking), Sourabh Ghosh (Head Consumer Banking), Abhay Kataria (Head Assets). Moderator: Chintan Shah, ICICI Securities
profile.subseg: JLG micro-loans; MBBL (micro-banking business loans); MSME (incl. Micro LAP); Housing; BBG (secured business banking); CV/CE (Wheels); CASA/term deposits

deepdive.sec: Financial Services — Small Finance Bank (SFB), micro-finance-led lender diversifying into secured retail/MSME

bull_bear.body:
- Rights issue of ₹950cr completed Nov-2025 to strengthen Tier-1 capital.
- ARC sale of stressed JLG portfolio executed to clean up legacy stress off the balance sheet.
- No immediate plans for further equity capital raise (CRAR 17.7%); if a shortfall emerges, management prefers Tier-2 capital or balance-sheet monetization over tapping equity markets.
- Reverse merger of holding company UCL into the bank in progress (NCLT process).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Legacy MFI/JLG stress still being provided for: 85% and ~70% provisioning stages still remaining on some aging buckets per CRO — implies further (declining) provisioning drag over the next couple of quarters.
- Wheels (CV/CE) segment remains the main source of non-MFI slippages (~4%); expected to normalize only over "another 2 quarters."
- ECL/Ind AS transition: SFBs currently exempted (implementation from 1-Apr-2027 excludes SFBs); management notes its own pro-forma Ind AS provisioning could be equal to or higher than current levels when/if it eventually applies — a future overhang, not immediate.
- Geopolitical: management monitored Iran-Israel/Middle East tensions (~2.5 months) for MSME export-exposure risk; states no abnormal portfolio behavior seen so far (ticket sizes too small for meaningful export/forex exposure).
- Credit-cost guidance (3–3.5% FY27, 2–2.5% FY28) explicitly reiterated (not raised) despite improving trends — management calling its own guidance "conservative," a point to verify against actuals.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Candid and granular in Q&A (specific PCR splits by book, SARFAESI timelines, LTV/risk-weight detail, opex-per-growth math). Repeated emphasis on **not** having booked any accounting/capital benefit yet from CGFMU cover — a conservative disclosure stance. Tone: cautiously confident ("worst is behind us"), explicitly reframing FY27 as consolidation rather than re-acceleration, which reads as credible expectation-setting rather than promotional.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The ₹56cr reported vs ~₹140cr adjusted PPoP gap (FY26) is a clean, quantified bridge management gave unprompted — useful reconciliation item for modeling next year's PPoP recovery.
- CGFMU cover (~70% of MFI book) is running as a pure cost today (premium expensed, zero benefit taken in NPA recognition or capital adequacy) — a hidden capital/provisioning optionality if/when claims mature (~1.5-year claim cycle per management).
- Reverse merger of parent UCL into the bank is progressing (NCLT 2nd motion filed Apr-2026) — corporate-structure simplification event to track for completion timing.
- Collection headcount (1,200+) is a temporary asset being explicitly repurposed toward write-off/NPA recovery (not just fresh-slippage collection) as normalization completes — an underappreciated future "collection ROI" lever (₹50cr recovered in Q4FY26 alone from ~900 people).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Equity has been raised twice in the public phase: IPO in Jul-23 to raise Rs 500 crore, oversubscribed >100x, and a Rights Issue "for an amount aggregating to Rs 950 crore in Nov-25".
- Capital position as on Jun-26: Net worth (Capital + Reserves) Rs 2,745 crore, CRAR 17.44%, Tier-I 15.13%, Tier-II 2.31%, on Risk Weighted Assets of Rs 14,373 crore.
- Book Value Per Share has been reset by losses and dilution: Mar'22 Rs 17.6, Mar'23 Rs 22.3, Mar'24 Rs 27.0, Mar'25 Rs 27.0, Mar'26 Rs 15.6, Jun'26 Rs 15.4.
- Balance sheet is deposit-funded and deleveraging on borrowings: Total balance sheet Rs 28,418 crore, Deposits Rs 22,054 crore (+3% YoY), Borrowings Rs 1,845 crore (-16% YoY, -35% QoQ) as on 30 June 2026.
- Shareholding as on 30 June 2026: Promoter (Utkarsh CoreInvest Limited) 42.7%, Individuals & Others 27.4%, FPI 11.9%, Insurance Companies 7.1%, Bodies Corporate 4.7%, Foreign Companies/NRIs 3.7%, AIFs 2.4%, Mutual Funds 0.0%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **MSME**: book +15% YoY to ₹4,456cr; new Micro LAP sub-segment yielding ~18% disbursement; MSME GNPA improved to 3.4% (from 3.6% prior quarter); largely secured by hard collateral (residential/commercial).
- **Housing**: +8% YoY to ₹990cr.
- **BBG (Business Banking Group)**: fully secured against immovable collateral, +19% YoY.
- **CV/CE ("Wheels")**: book -1% QoQ to ₹1,090cr; deliberate mix shift toward used vehicles (share of disbursements ~30% in FY26 vs <15% a year ago) as new-vehicle financing was showing riskier behaviour; Wheels remains the main driver of elevated non-MFI slippages (~4%), expected to normalize over "at least another 2 quarters."
- **Deposits**: total deposits +0.4% YoY / ~+3% QoQ (broadly stable by design); retail term deposits +20% YoY; CASA +11% YoY/+13% QoQ; CASA+RTD ratio 83% (Mar-26) vs 71% (Mar-25); CASA ratio 24%.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- CGFMU credit-guarantee coverage: ~70% of the microfinance book (counting Q4FY26 disbursements) now covered under the credit-guarantee scheme (registered effective 17-Jan-2025) — reduces incremental portfolio risk on new MFI-book originations; management stresses no accounting/capital benefit has yet been booked from this cover (pure cost so far), so any future claim/capital-relief is unrecognized upside.
- Deep micro-finance underwriting experience (per management) supporting confidence in resuming 25-30% growth from a low base without repeating past credit-cost cycles.

business.body:
- "One of the Largest Banking Network Amongst SFBs - >1,100 banking outlets well-entrenched across the country; ~25% GB branches in growth phase  significant growth potential without further infrastructure investment."
- "Strategic Geographic Expansion: Sustaining JLG dominance in UP & Bihar on the back of first-mover advantage and brand recall, alongside retail lending expansion in new geographies for diversification."
- "Diversified Asset Mix within the SFBs - Swiftly de-risking the business with Secured loans now constituting 51% of the portfolio."
- "Significant presence in rural & semi urban locations and under penetrated States of the Country" - 88% of micro-banking branches are in rural and semi-urban locations; "Committed journey of ~16 years from Microfinance to Small Finance Bank to Listed Company".
- Franchise scale as of Jun-26: 5.32 million total customers, 1,110 banking outlets across 27 States & UTs, 373 ATMs, 789 Micro ATMs and 298 URCs; head count 18,136 vs 19,871 (Jun-25).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Asset quality] Legacy MFI stress is the dominant swing factor: GNPA 5.9% (Jun-26) vs 7.6% (Mar-26) vs 11.4% (Jun-25); NNPA 2.8% vs 3.2% vs 5.0%; PCR 54.6%; gross NPAs fell from Rs 2,196 Cr (Jun-25) to Rs 1,163 Cr (Jun-26), helped by ARC sales of Rs 624 Cr in Q4 FY26 and Rs 365 Cr in Q1 FY27 plus write-offs, not by recoveries alone (up-gradations & recoveries were Rs 69 Cr in Q1 FY27).
- [Asset quality] Micro-banking leading indicators have turned: collection efficiency (excl. pre-payments) rose from 82% (Q1'FY26) to 91% (Q1'FY27) and total SMA fell from 5.1% to 1.2% over Jun-25 to Jun-26; the deck states "Post-guardrail book demonstrating superior performance" and that "The collection force will be retained for legacy NPA book & write off collections".
- [Credit rating] Long-term rating A- (Stable) from ICRA and A- Stable from CARE, short-term Certificate of Deposit programme [ICRA] A1, with a footnote that "Credit Rating revised on Jul 2nd and 14th, 2026" - the deck does not state the direction of the revision or the prior rating.
- [Leadership] Sarjukumar Pravin Simaria joined as Executive Director w.e.f. June 22, 2026 (ex-Edelweiss, Fino Payments Bank, AIG, HDFC AMC); Govind Singh continues as MD & CEO, and the deck headlines "Leadership and Governance strengthening the Bank's core competencies".
- [Risk infrastructure] Underwriting has been rebuilt around a rules-engine-integrated Loan Origination System, scorecard-based evaluation with field visits, Hunter and Sherlock for fraud/adverse-history detection, Perfios for financial due diligence, and early-warning-signal monitoring.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Cost of funds down to 7.9% in Q4FY26 (from 8.3% in Q4FY25, 8.1% in Q3FY26) via calibrated deposit repricing after RBI repo cuts; further reduction expected as repricing continues. Reported FY26 PPoP (₹56cr) heavily suppressed by interest-income reversals from fresh slippages (~₹84cr across the year); management expects reversals to shrink as the new (post-guardrail) disbursement book performs and collection efficiency holds, allowing steady-state interest income to "find its revival" over the next ~4 quarters.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** Fresh slippages collapsed (~₹710cr→~₹170cr YoY); GNPA improved 330bps QoQ to 7.7%; JLG mix down to 28–30% of book; secured mix up to 51%; net loss ₹188cr on legacy provisioning; Rights issue (₹950cr, Nov-25) done; reverse merger (UCL into bank) filed with NCLT; FY27 framed as consolidation year; credit-cost guidance (3–3.5% FY27 / 2–2.5% FY28) and FY28 ROE >15% reiterated.
- **Q1 FY27 → check:** Did JLG/non-JLG disbursement momentum (+58%/+41% QoQ) continue or was Q4 a one-off low-base bounce? Did fresh slippages keep falling below ~₹170cr/qtr? Any progress on CBS launch (guided Q2/Q3 FY27) and NCLT reverse-merger completion? Any change to "no equity raise" stance despite 25–30% growth ambition?

outlook.body:
- **Loan book growth**: 25–30% p.a. over "coming years" (medium-term target reiterated on call).
- **Secured mix**: target ~55% of gross loan book (vs 51% now, 43% a year ago).
- **NIM**: >8% (medium-term target).
- **ROE**: ~15% target; FY28 exit ROE "above 15%" reconfirmed on this call (from prior-call guidance).
- **Credit cost**: reiterated from previous call — ~3–3.5% FY27, 2–2.5% FY28 (management flags this as conservative given slippage trajectory and CGFMU cover).
- **Net NPA**: <1% by FY28 (from ~3.3% in FY26).
- **New CBS (core banking system)** launch targeted Q2/Q3 FY27 (part of "Utkarsh 2.0" tech transformation).
- **Capital raise**: no immediate equity capital raise planned; if needed, will use Tier-2 or balance-sheet monetization, not equity market.
- **Reverse merger** (holding co. UCL into the bank): 2nd motion petition filed with NCLT 5-Apr-2026; expected to complete "in the next few months," subject to NCLT.
- FY27 explicitly framed as a **consolidation year** — converting Q4FY26 green shoots into sustained momentum, not a growth-acceleration year.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Disbursement momentum turning: JLG disbursements +58% QoQ (+2% YoY) to ₹1,310cr in Q4FY26 — first QoQ increase after 3 consecutive quarters of decline — as collections stabilized (~Oct/Nov-25) and sales focus resumed under MFIN 2.0 guardrails; management still describes disbursal capacity as running at only ~70% of optimum, implying further upside. Non-JLG disbursements +41% QoQ / +51% YoY. MBBL (graduating-JLG secured-adjacent product) +122% YoY / +40% QoQ, now 27% of micro-banking book with <15% penetration — flagged as the biggest headroom item.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- MBBL scale-up (27% of micro-banking book, <15% penetration) — largest identified growth lever within the de-risked JLG-graduate segment.
- Gold Loan — new-ish product, management expects meaningfully bigger scale this year.
- Micro LAP (within MSME) — ~18% yield, early-stage.
- Post-Q3FY26 write-off/NPA recovery vertical: ~30% of the 1,200+ collection headcount to be redeployed toward legacy write-off/NPA collection once fresh-slippage normalization completes; ₹50cr collected from NPA/write-off pool in Q4FY26 alone (~20% of collected value via a ~900-person team then).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: FY26 was a deliberate de-risking year: JLG (microfinance) book cut from ~88% of loans (FY20) to ~28-30% now, secured lending raised to 51% of book, and legacy MFI stress (post the ~1.5-year MFIN 2.0 guardrail shock) is now clearing — fresh slippages fell from ~₹710cr (Q4FY25) to ~₹170cr (Q4FY26) and GNPA improved ~330bps QoQ to 7.7%. Bank still posted a Q4 net loss of ₹188cr on legacy provisioning, but management calls "worst behind us," guides to FY27 as a consolidation year and FY28 exit ROE >15%.
